items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Cab said, 'Foots, did you do something on 'Minnie The Moocher'?'

ctx.x: No, not Fred Coots. We're talking about some of the guys who... Oh, I used to take his name with me all the time. I generally take a book and look in it. But anyway, he could tell... I never recorded with nobody that had such an ear like him. He could tell which saxophone player squeaked. If he knew your reeds weren't quite wet and you squeaked, he could hear the first saxophone squeak, and he'd stop you in the middle of a recording. Because he wouldn't let... You had to go through it all the way in and start…

So we started playing this arrangement this guy made, and it just wasn't makin' no sense. So Cab... After about three or four times playing this other arrangement, Cab said, "Foots, did you do something on 'Minnie The Moocher'?" I said, "Yes." So I went to my little saxophone case and got out my little strips of paper, and passed them around. We didn't have but ten pieces in it, the same band he... So we started playing that.
